title: Follow the menu
brief:
Write the whole test this time. Starting on the home page:

1. click the **Products** link in the menu
2. check the address is `https://automationexercise.com/products`
3. check the **All Products** heading is on screen

Two assertions, because they prove different things: one that you *navigated*, one that the page actually *rendered*.

For the heading, `get_by_role("heading", name="All Products")` reads better than any CSS selector - it finds it the way a person would.
starter:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_products_page_opens_from_the_menu(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/")

    # Your turn: click, then check twice.
solution:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_products_page_opens_from_the_menu(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/")

    page.get_by_role("link", name="Products").click()

    expect(page).to_have_url("https://automationexercise.com/products")
    expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name="All Products")).to_be_visible()

checks.label: The shop ends up on the products page
checks.feedback: The shop is still somewhere else. Did the click find the Products link in the menu?

checks.name: to_have_url
checks.label: You assert the address
checks.feedback: No to_have_url check ran. Remember it goes on the page: expect(page).to_have_url(...).

checks.name: to_be_visible
checks.label: You assert the heading is visible
checks.feedback: No to_be_visible check ran. If your assertion is below a line that failed, it never got the chance - fix the first failure and run again.

checks.name: role
checks.label: You used role-based locators (the top of the priority list)
checks.feedback: You got there, but with a CSS selector where a role locator would do. get_by_role finds elements the way a user does, so it survives redesigns that break a class name. Try get_by_role("link", name="Products") and get_by_role("heading", name="All Products").

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: Three lines: one click, two expects. The click is a link; the heading is a heading.

hints.label: Strategy
hints.text: page.get_by_role("link", name="Products").click(), then expect(page).to_have_url("https://automationexercise.com/products"), then expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name="All Products")).to_be_visible().

reveal:
Notice you never told Playwright to *wait* for the products page. `to_have_url` and `to_be_visible` retry on their own until the page catches up.

That is the habit this whole quest is built around, and it is why the kit's rule is: **never `time.sleep()`**.
